newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber stable in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber stable in late trading.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 offer prices were stable in late trading on Friday with rupiah movements the main issue in the market, traders said.
They said a deal was done overnight at 42.00 U.S. cents/lb fob Palembang for October shipment and at 42.25 fob Medan.
Offer prices were quoted at 43.00 fob Medan for November shipment, 41.50 fob Padang, Pontianak and Jambi for September shipment and 42.00 fob Surabaya. Traders offered rubber at 42.00 fob Surabaya.
"This market has been very gloomy. First, demand was very weak, and now the rupiah trouble. Buyers have anticipated that prices will decline," said one trader in Palembang, South Sumatra.
The rupiah fell to a historic low of 2,915 against the dollar in afternoon trading following the central bank's move on Thursday to scrap its intervention band.
Rubber traders said there was some concern that Thailand might sell its excess stocks, which currently stand at about 70,000 tonnes.

"It's an old issue that Thailand will sell its stocks, but this also contributed to the weak market sentiment. Now, dealers are taking a wait-and-see position to await further developments," said one trader.
"We expect to see a clearer picture on what the currency is going to be next week. We also expect the market to be weak," he added.
Some traders said they believed buyers would enter the market when levels dropped to 40.00 U.S. cents.
"I think that level is a kind of resistance level in which buyers will have no choice but to buy rubber," said one trader.
